rows.verified: Metalworking-fluid exposure can cause dermatitis, occupational asthma, hypersensitivity pneumonitis and other respiratory illness.
Exposure can occur by inhaling mist, direct skin contact, broken skin and poor hygiene.
COSHH requires metalworking-fluid exposure to be prevented where reasonably practicable or otherwise adequately controlled.
CNC machining guidance uses enclosure and engineering controls to reduce airborne mist exposure.
Health surveillance is required where exposure to fluid or mist cannot be prevented.
Fluid quality and bacterial contamination should be monitored and maintained.
HSE and industry guidance prioritises prevention of work-related asthma and dermatitis from metalworking fluids.
Fluid chemistry and contamination should be controlled to limit formation of hazardous nitrosamines and polycyclic aromatics.
Metalworking-fluid risk depends on formulation, mist generation, bacterial load, enclosure, extraction, skin contact, maintenance and exposure duration.
HSE metalworking-fluid evidence is fluid-, machine-, task-, worker-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level disease probability.
A biological agent may cause infection, allergy, toxicity or another hazard to human health.
Incidental occupational exposure can involve blood, body fluids, contaminated water, waste, bedding, animals and metalworking fluids.
Employers must assess biological-agent risks and control them under COSHH.
Deliberate work with biological agents requires classification, risk assessment and suitable containment measures.
Laboratory and production work with Hazard Group agents may require notification, clearance or consent.
Exposure routes include skin or mucous-membrane contact, inhalation, ingestion and inoculation through sharps injury.
Emergency arrangements should address accidental releases capable of causing severe disease or spread to others.
Risk assessment must consider transmission routes and individual vulnerability including immune compromise and pregnancy.
Biological-agent risk depends on agent, hazard group, route, dose, task, containment, worker susceptibility and emergency readiness.
HSE biological-agent evidence is agent-, task-, workplace-, worker-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
